shared_elements: circular/disc motif (a plain disc on A, rosettes and spiralled horns on B)
horizontal banding or register lines dividing the surface
justification: Both are stone surfaces worked in shallow relief and both organise their motifs against horizontal dividing lines, with a prominent disc/rosette form in each, but that is about as specific as the overlap gets. A is a free-standing, boulder-like vertical block with heavily eroded, abstract and symmetrical emblems stacked one above another, while B is a flat, finely finished panel carrying a naturalistic horizontal procession of figures and animals with a rosette border — utterly different in format, subject and quality of execution.
